title: Deleted, still showing
fullTitle: I Deleted the Record. Why Is It Still Showing Up?

scenes.narration: We deleted contact one zero zero three. The record lookup says four oh four. Yet search still returns Dana Whitlock, and so does the page already open.
captions: Record lookup: 404. Search: still returns c_1003.
The open results page still shows her too.

scenes.narration: One contact, four homes: the primary table, a search index with a denormalised copy, an application response cache, and the browser's already-fetched results.
captions: Primary table, search index, response cache, open browser.

scenes.narration: The flawed delete stops after the primary row. Nothing records that other copies need cleaning, so the index and cached response still return her.
captions: Flawed delete: primary row only. Outbox events: 0.
Index and cached response still return c_1003.

scenes.narration: The fix: one transaction deletes the primary row and inserts a deletion event into the outbox. A local worker removes the index entry and clears the whole directory cache. The outbox records cleanup intent; it does not make every destination update atomically.
captions: One transaction: delete the row and insert the outbox event.
The outbox records intent. It is not atomic across destinations.

scenes.narration: A deliberate fault: the index entry is removed, then cache invalidation fails. The event stays pending, and the cache keeps serving the old answer until invalidation succeeds.
captions: Index entry removed. Cache invalidation fails once.
Event stays pending. The cache still serves c_1003.

scenes.narration: The worker retries. Attempt two clears the cache, and only then is the event processed. Replaying it changes nothing, and the ID is never reused. If retries run out, the event becomes failed and raises an alert.
captions: Attempt two succeeds. Processed only after both steps.
Replay is safe. Exhausted retries: failed state and alert.

scenes.narration: Verify both backend copies: primary record gone, index entry gone, and no cached response mentions the contact.
captions: Backend verified: primary, index and cache are clean.

scenes.narration: The simulated open page still shows her: a server cannot recall data the client already holds. Only a refresh fetches again, and then she disappears.
captions: The open page keeps its old results until it fetches again.

scenes.narration: Deletion is a workflow when data has more than one home. This is not a privacy-erasure system: backups, logs, exports and third-party copies are out of scope, and deletion never retrieves what was already downloaded.
captions: Deletion is a workflow when data has more than one home.
Not a privacy-erasure system. Backups, logs, exports, third parties: out of scope.
